deities: Goddess Kali (presiding deity of the Lower Dobasipara shrine - inferred from its name; the shrine itself is undocumented in published sources)

history.summary: The CSV name 'Kali Temple, Tura' is generic and cannot be pinned to a single shrine with certainty: Tura and the wider West Garo Hills have several documented Kali shrines - Lower Dobasipara Kali Mandir (Tura), Shiv Kali Mandir (Barengapara), Rishi Para Kalibari (Tura, Mondol Barrack Road), Kaimbatapara Kali Mandir (Bamundanga) and Millonpur Kali Mandir - and none of them has any published history, festival record or news coverage. BEST-SUPPORTED REFERENT: this file is anchored to the Lower Dobasipara Kali Mandir in Tura (approx. 25.5069N, 90.2115E from geocoding), the only Kali shrine geocoded within Tura town with high confidence, but the CSV may equally intend one of the other Kali shrines, so identity is PROVISIONAL. Nothing about the shrine's age, builder or rituals is documented; treat as a placeholder pending local verification. CSV town and state are correct (Tura, Meghalaya); district filled in as West Garo Hills. No reliable image of the shrine was found after genuine searching, so media is intentionally empty.

name: Kali Temple
town_description: Tura is a municipality and the district headquarters of West Garo Hills district in western Meghalaya, set in the foothills of the Tura Hills below Tura Peak, near Nokrek National Park. One of Meghalaya's largest towns and the cultural and administrative centre of the Garo tribe, it is the road gateway to the Garo Hills' tourist spots (Balpakram, Nokrek, Siju Cave) and lies about 220 km from Guwahati and 323 km from Shillong. The town's Hindu minority maintains small local shrines alongside its many churches.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism - inferred from the name; unverified)

travel.airport: Nearest airport with scheduled commercial flights: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, Assam (approx. 155-180 km by road; verify). Rupsi Airport (Assam) is closer (approx. 76-85 km per aggregators; verify) but has limited scheduled services (verify).
travel.railway: Nearest railheads: Dhubri (Assam, per travel aggregators; verify) and Mendipathar (North Garo Hills; verify); Guwahati is the nearest major rail junction (approx. 180-200 km by road; verify).
travel.road: Tura is the road hub of the Garo Hills, linked by highway to Guwahati (approx. 180-220 km; verify) and Shillong (approx. 323 km per travel guides; verify); local travel by shared sumo, taxi and auto.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather in the Garo Hills (verify locally). Kali Puja (October-November) is the shrine's likely main festival (verify - not documented for this shrine specifically).
